mcqs.learning_point: Understand the mathematical idea of a point
mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes a geometric point?

options.C: It has no dimension; it is only a location.
options.D: It can be measured with a ruler.

mcqs.answer: It has no dimension; it is only a location.
mcqs.explanation: A point in geometry is defined as an exact location in space and has no length, width, or height. Therefore option C is correct. Options A, B, and D incorrectly attribute size or measurability to a point, which is a common misconception.

mcqs.learning_point: Represent a point using a labelled dot
mcqs.question: In a diagram a dot is labelled with the letter P. Which notation correctly represents that point?
mcqs.explanation: A point is denoted simply by a capital letter without any surrounding symbols. Hence the correct representation is just the letter P. The other options add brackets or parentheses, which are not used for points in standard geometric notation.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand a line as extending indefinitely in both directions
mcqs.question: How does a line differ from a line segment?

options.B: A line has no endpoints, while a line segment has two distinct endpoints.
options.C: A line is of finite length, whereas a line segment is infinite.
options.D: A line segment extends indefinitely in both directions.

mcqs.answer: A line has no endpoints, while a line segment has two distinct endpoints.
mcqs.explanation: By definition, a line continues without end in both directions and therefore has no endpoints. A line segment, on the other hand, is bounded by two endpoints. Options A, C, and D incorrectly describe the properties of lines and segments.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand a ray as having one endpoint and extending indefinitely in one direction
mcqs.question: Ray AB is drawn on a coordinate plane. Which description accurately characterises this ray?

options.A: It starts at point B and passes through A, extending infinitely beyond B.
options.B: It starts at point A and passes through B, extending infinitely beyond B.
options.C: It has endpoints at both A and B.
options.D: It is the same as the line passing through A and B.

mcqs.answer: It starts at point A and passes through B, extending infinitely beyond B.
mcqs.explanation: A ray is defined by an endpoint (the starting point) and a direction. Ray AB begins at A, goes through B, and continues without bound past B. Option A reverses the endpoint, option C incorrectly gives two endpoints, and option D confuses a ray with a line, which has no endpoint.
